applicability_basis.quote: This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard.
6 Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).

assumptions: Application assumes the fund falls within the circular’s definition of Funds and is not a LAF.
The selected actor is understood as the fund or its management company for the classification question.
Operative provision describes the circular’s prescriptive text; its independent statutory force is not established.
authorities.proposition: A covered Fund must be classified as a complex product when its combined direct and indirect exposure to private market assets reaches or exceeds 50% of NAV. Exactly 50% meets the threshold. Exposure alone below that threshold does not establish mandatory classification under this rule.
relevant_factors: SFC authorisation for public offering in Hong Kong

role_basis.quote: A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV.
private credit and private equity (collectively, private market assets)

applicability_basis.quote: 7 In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.

assumptions: No actual case-specific designation is supplied.
The listed factors inform discretion; no individual factor is stated to compel designation.
authorities.proposition: Below 50% aggregate exposure, the SFC may designate a covered Fund as complex after a holistic, case-specific assessment. Falling below 50% therefore does not establish non-complex status.
relevant_factors: Extent, nature and characteristics of specific asset types
SRT structure, tranches and underlying assets
Home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions
Other relevant circumstances; the factors are non-exhaustive

role_basis.quote: On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
the aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets of the Fund;
the Fund's overall investment strategy, portfolio composition, and liquidity and/or risk profile;
the extent, nature and characteristics of the specific asset types in which the Fund invests (eg, the tranches and credit ratings of CLOs; the structure, tranches and underlying assets of SRTs); and
any distribution restrictions, requirements or other conditions as may be imposed by the Fund’s home regulators.

applicability_basis.quote: For existing SFC-authorised funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, fund managers are expected to undertake a review of their funds, take appropriate actions including updating the Fund’s offering documents as soon as practicable, and ensure necessary and proper communications with the distributors in light of the guidance provided under this circular (in particular, with respect to paragraphs 9 and 10 above).

assumptions: Application assumes an existing covered Fund with possible private-market exposure.
Missing classification evidence is uncertainty, not evidence that the Fund is non-complex.

authorities.proposition: Managers of existing covered Funds with possible private-market exposure are expected to review their funds, take appropriate action and communicate with distributors. They are encouraged to consult the SFC promptly when classification is doubtful. The supplied source does not classify any particular Fund.

applicability_basis.quote: Funds with direct or indirect exposure to private market assets are required to observe the enhanced disclosure requirements set out in this circular.

assumptions: Disclosure obligations and investment limits are distinct from the complex-product classification test.
The UT Code itself has not been supplied; its complete scope and exceptions remain unverified.
authorities.proposition: Enhanced disclosure applies to covered Funds with direct or indirect private-market exposure without a stated 50% threshold. The circular separately reports a 15% NAV investment limit for direct private-asset investments or exposures under UT Code 7.3. Neither provision substitutes for the aggregate 50% classification rule or eliminates discretionary designation below 50%.
relevant_factors: Enhanced disclosure is not itself a complex-product designation
15% limit concerns direct investments or exposures
50% classification threshold aggregates direct and indirect exposures
Examples of indirect exposures are non-exhaustive

role_basis.quote: Funds with direct or indirect exposure to private market assets are required to observe the enhanced disclosure requirements set out in this circular.
1 Direct investments in/exposures to private assets fall within the investment limit of 15% of a Fund’s total net asset value (NAV) under 7.3 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds (UT Code).
2 The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.
